excerpt: To determine whether the measures we have adopted satisfy the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, we will conduct a safeguards assessment.
paraphrase: Anthropic will conduct a safeguards assessment to check whether its measures meet the ASL-3 Required Safeguards.

excerpt: As noted, the Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold are specified in Section 2.
paraphrase: The Required Safeguards for each Capability Threshold appear in Section 2.

excerpt: We will document our implementation of the Required Safeguards in a Safeguards Report.
paraphrase: Implementation of the Required Safeguards will be documented in a Safeguards Report.

excerpt: Currently, these will be informal estimates of (1) the extent to which widely available elicitation techniques may improve and (2) how the model will perform on the same tasks when the next round of testing begins.
paraphrase: For now, forecasts will be informal estimates covering elicitation technique improvement and future task performance.

excerpt: As these are open research questions, we will aim to improve these forecasts over time so that they can be relied upon for risk judgments.
paraphrase: Because these are open research questions, forecasts will be improved over time to support risk judgments.

excerpt: In the case where the capability assessment shows a model is just barely below the threshold, the Responsible Scaling Officer may choose to limit further training to some amount less than the default 4x Effective Compute increase until ASL-3 measures are in place, in order to limit risk.
paraphrase: If a model is just barely below the threshold, the Responsible Scaling Officer may cap further training below the default 4x Effective Compute increase until ASL-3 measures are ready.

excerpt: There may be a substantial period during which models are not demonstrably close to the Capability Threshold, but we nevertheless are unable to rule out the risk to our satisfaction, and thus choose to implement the Required Safeguards.
paraphrase: Even when models are not clearly close to the Capability Threshold, Anthropic may implement Required Safeguards if it cannot rule out the risk to its satisfaction.

excerpt: When a model must meet the ASL-3 Deployment Standard, we will evaluate whether the measures we have implemented make us robust to persistent attempts to misuse the capability in question.
paraphrase: When the ASL-3 Deployment Standard applies, Anthropic will evaluate whether its measures make it robust to persistent misuse attempts.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Lead-in stating that several criteria must be satisfied to demonstrate the standard is met.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat modeling: Make a compelling case that the set of threats and the vectors through which an adversary could catastrophically misuse the deployed system have been sufficiently mapped out, and will commit to revising as necessary over time.
paraphrase: Anthropic must convincingly show threats and misuse vectors have been mapped and commit to revising the threat model over time.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Defense in depth: Use a "defense in depth" approach by building a series of defensive layers, each designed to catch misuse attempts that might pass through previous barriers.
paraphrase: A layered defensive approach must be used, with each layer designed to catch misuse attempts that pass earlier layers.

excerpt: As an example, this might entail achieving a high overall recall rate using harm refusal techniques. This is an area of active research, and new technologies may be added when ready.
paraphrase: An example is high recall via harm refusal techniques; this is active research and new technologies may be added later.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Red-teaming: Conduct red-teaming that demonstrates that threat actors with realistic access levels and resources are highly unlikely to be able to consistently elicit information from any generally accessible systems that greatly increases their ability to cause catastrophic harm relative to other available tools.
paraphrase: Red-teaming must show realistic threat actors are highly unlikely to extract catastrophic-harm-enabling information beyond what other tools already provide.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Rapid remediation: Show that any compromises of the deployed system, such as jailbreaks or other attack pathways, will be identified and remediated promptly enough to prevent the overall system from meaningfully increasing an adversary's ability to cause catastrophic harm.
paraphrase: Must demonstrate compromises like jailbreaks will be identified and fixed quickly enough to prevent meaningful uplift to adversaries.

excerpt: Example techniques could include rapid vulnerability patching, the ability to escalate to law enforcement when appropriate, and any necessary retention of logs for these activities.
paraphrase: Example techniques include rapid patching, law enforcement escalation, and log retention.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Monitoring: Prespecify empirical evidence that would show the system is operating within the accepted risk range and define a process for reviewing the system's performance on a reasonable cadence.
paraphrase: Must prespecify evidence showing acceptable risk range operation and define a periodic review process.

excerpt: Process examples include monitoring responses to jailbreak bounties, doing historical analysis or background monitoring, and any necessary retention of logs for these activities.
paraphrase: Example processes include jailbreak bounty monitoring, historical/background analysis, and log retention.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Trusted users: Establish criteria for determining when it may be appropriate to share a version of the model with reduced safeguards with trusted users. In addition, demonstrate that an alternative set of controls will provide equivalent levels of assurance.
paraphrase: Must set criteria for sharing reduced-safeguard versions with trusted users and show alternative controls give equivalent assurance.

excerpt: This could include a sufficient combination of user vetting, secure access controls, monitoring, log retention, and incident response protocols.
paraphrase: Could include user vetting, secure access controls, monitoring, log retention, and incident response protocols.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Must document how models meet the above criteria even when deployed in third-party environments with different safeguards.

excerpt: When a model must meet the ASL-3 Security Standard, we will evaluate whether the measures we have implemented make us highly protected against most attackers' attempts at stealing model weights.
paraphrase: When the ASL-3 Security Standard applies, Anthropic will evaluate whether it is highly protected against most weight-theft attempts.

excerpt: This criterion does not attempt to specify the exact red-teaming protocol (e.g., number of hours, level of access, or pass-fail criteria). Setting a principled pass-fail threshold will depend on other factors, such as the quality of our monitoring and ability to respond to jailbreaks rapidly.
paraphrase: The red-teaming criterion leaves protocol details unspecified; the pass-fail threshold depends on monitoring quality and rapid response ability.

excerpt: Due to the likely ease of bypassing or removing safeguards via fine-tuning, it may be difficult or impossible for these red-teaming tests to pass if weights are released or if unmoderated fine-tuning access is provided to untrusted users.
paraphrase: Red-teaming tests may be very hard to pass if weights are released or unmoderated fine-tuning access is given to untrusted users, since safeguards can be easily bypassed via fine-tuning.

excerpt: We consider the following groups in scope: hacktivists, criminal hacker groups, organized cybercrime groups, terrorist organizations, corporate espionage teams, internal employees, and state-sponsored programs that use broad-based and non-targeted techniques (i.e., not novel attack chains).
paraphrase: In-scope threat actors include hacktivists, criminal groups, terrorists, corporate espionage teams, insiders, and state-sponsored programs using non-targeted techniques.

excerpt: The following groups are out of scope for the ASL-3 Security Standard because further testing (as discussed below) should confirm that the model would not meaningfully increase their ability to do harm:
paraphrase: Lead-in identifying groups excluded from ASL-3 Security Standard scope, pending further testing confirmation.

context_stem: Groups out of scope for ASL-3 Security Standard
excerpt: state-sponsored programs that specifically target us (e.g., through novel attack chains or insider compromise) and a small number (~10) of non-state actors with state-level resourcing or backing that are capable of developing novel attack chains that utilize 0-day attacks.
paraphrase: Out-of-scope actors are state programs specifically targeting Anthropic and roughly ten non-state actors with state-level resources capable of novel zero-day attack chains.

excerpt: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
paraphrase: Lead-in stating criteria to be satisfied for the ASL-3 Security Standard.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Threat modeling: Follow risk governance best practices, such as use of the MITRE ATT&CK Framework to establish the relationship between the identified threats, sensitive assets, attack vectors and, in doing so, sufficiently capture the resulting risks that must be addressed to protect model weights from theft attempts.
paraphrase: Must follow risk governance best practices such as MITRE ATT&CK to map threats, assets, and vectors and capture the risks to weight security.

excerpt: As part of this requirement, we should specify our plans for revising the resulting threat model over time.
paraphrase: Must also specify plans for revising the threat model over time.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Security frameworks: Align to and, as needed, extend industry-standard security frameworks for addressing identified risks, such as disclosure of sensitive information, tampering with accounts and assets, and unauthorized elevation of privileges with the appropriate controls.
paraphrase: Must align with and extend industry-standard security frameworks to address risks like data disclosure, tampering, and privilege escalation.

excerpt: This includes:
paraphrase: Lead-in to sub-items of the security frameworks criterion.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and extend industry-standard security frameworks. This includes:
excerpt: Perimeters and access controls: Building strong perimeters and access controls around sensitive assets to ensure AI models and critical systems are protected from unauthorized access.
paraphrase: Sub-criterion requiring strong perimeters and access controls protecting AI models and critical systems from unauthorized access.

excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of physical security, encryption, cloud security, infrastructure policy, access management, and weight access minimization and monitoring.
paraphrase: Expected components include physical security, encryption, cloud security, infrastructure policy, access management, and weight access minimization/monitoring.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and extend industry-standard security frameworks. This includes:
excerpt: Lifecycle security: Securing links in the chain of systems and software used to develop models, to prevent compromised components from being introduced and to ensure only trusted code and hardware is used.
paraphrase: Sub-criterion requiring securing of the development supply chain against compromised components and untrusted code/hardware.

excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of software inventory, supply chain security, artifact integrity, binary authorization, hardware procurement, and secure research development lifecycle.
paraphrase: Expected components include software inventory, supply chain security, artifact integrity, binary authorization, hardware procurement, and secure R&D lifecycle.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and extend industry-standard security frameworks. This includes:
excerpt: Monitoring: Proactively identifying and mitigating threats through ongoing and effective monitoring, testing for vulnerabilities, and laying traps for potential attackers.
paraphrase: Sub-criterion requiring proactive threat identification/mitigation via monitoring, vulnerability testing, and attacker traps.

excerpt: We expect this will include a combination of endpoint patching, product security testing, log management, asset monitoring, and intruder deception techniques.
paraphrase: Expected components include endpoint patching, product security testing, log management, asset monitoring, and intruder deception techniques.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and extend industry-standard security frameworks. This includes:
excerpt: Resourcing: Investing sufficient resources in security.
paraphrase: Sub-criterion requiring sufficient investment of resources in security.

excerpt: We expect meeting this standard of security to require roughly 5-10% of employees being dedicated to security and security-adjacent work.
paraphrase: Meeting the security standard is expected to require about 5-10% of employees dedicated to security-related work.

context_stem: Security frameworks: Align to and extend industry-standard security frameworks. This includes:
excerpt: Existing guidance: Aligning where appropriate with existing guidance on securing model weights, including Securing AI Model Weights, Preventing Theft and Misuse of Frontier Models (2024); security recommendations like Deploying AI Systems Securely (CISA/NSA/FBI/ASD/CCCS/GCSB /GCHQ), ISO 42001, CSA's AI Safety Initiative, and CoSAI; and standards frameworks like SSDF, SOC 2, NIST 800-53.
paraphrase: Sub-criterion requiring alignment with named existing guidance and standards frameworks on securing model weights.

excerpt: We will implement robust insider risk controls to mitigate most insider risk, but consider mitigating risks from highly sophisticated state-compromised insiders to be out of scope for ASL-3.
paraphrase: Robust insider risk controls will be implemented, but mitigating highly sophisticated state-compromised insider risks is out of scope for ASL-3.

excerpt: We are committed to further enhancing these protections as a part of our ASL-4 preparations.
paraphrase: Anthropic commits to further enhancing insider risk protections as part of ASL-4 preparations.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Audits: Develop plans to (1) audit and assess the design and implementation of the security program and (2) share these findings (and updates on any remediation efforts) with management on an appropriate cadence.
paraphrase: Must develop plans to audit the security program and share findings and remediation updates with management periodically.

excerpt: We expect this to include independent validation of threat modeling and risk assessment results; a sampling-based audit of the operating effectiveness of the defined controls; periodic, broadly scoped, and independent testing with expert red-teamers who are industry-renowned and have been recognized in competitive challenges.
paraphrase: Expected audit elements include independent threat model/risk validation, sampling-based control audits, and periodic independent red-team testing by renowned experts.

context_stem: To make the required showing, we will need to satisfy the following criteria:
excerpt: Third-party environments: Document how all relevant models will meet the criteria above, even if they are deployed in a third-party partner's environment that may have a different set of safeguards.
paraphrase: Must document how models meet the above criteria even in third-party environments with different safeguards.

excerpt: If, after the evaluations above, we determine that we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards, then we may proceed with deploying and training models above the Capability Threshold, provided we have also conducted a follow-up capability assessment.
paraphrase: If the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are determined to be met, deployment and training above the Capability Threshold may proceed, provided a follow-up capability assessment is conducted.

excerpt: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
paraphrase: Lead-in introducing the process for determining whether the Required Safeguards have been met.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: First, we will compile a Safeguards Report for each Required Safeguard that documents our implementation of the measures above, makes an affirmative case for why we have satisfied them, and advances recommendations on deployment decisions.
paraphrase: A Safeguards Report will first be compiled for each Required Safeguard, documenting implementation, making a case for satisfaction, and recommending deployment decisions.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: The Safeguards Report(s) will be escalated to the CEO and the Responsible Scaling Officer, who will (1) make the ultimate determination as to whether we have satisfied the Required Safeguards and (2) decide any deployment-related issues.
paraphrase: The Safeguards Report will go to the CEO and RSO, who make the final determination of compliance and decide deployment issues.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: In general, as noted in Sections 7.1.4 and 7.2.2, we will solicit both internal and external expert feedback on the report as well as the CEO and RSO's conclusions to inform future refinements to our methodology.
paraphrase: Internal and external expert feedback will generally be solicited on the report and conclusions to inform future methodology refinements.

excerpt: For high-stakes issues, however, the CEO and RSO will likely solicit internal and external feedback on the report prior to making any decisions.
paraphrase: For high-stakes issues, feedback will likely be solicited before decisions are made.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: If the CEO and RSO decide to proceed with deployment and training, they will share their decision–as well as the underlying Safeguards Report, internal feedback, and any external feedback–with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust before moving forward.
paraphrase: If proceeding with deployment/training, the CEO and RSO will share the decision and supporting materials with the Board and Long-Term Benefit Trust first.

context_stem: The process for determining whether we have met the ASL-3 Required Safeguards is as follows:
excerpt: After the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are approved, they will be revisited and re-approved at least annually to re-affirm their suitability and sound implementation.
paraphrase: Once approved, the Required Safeguards will be reviewed and re-approved at least once a year.

excerpt: If, however, we are unable to make the showing required above, we will restrict model deployment and further scaling.
paraphrase: If the required showing cannot be made, model deployment and further scaling will be restricted.

excerpt: In parallel with upgrading a model to the Required Safeguards, we will (1) update this policy to include any additional Capability Thresholds for which the Required Safeguards would be insufficient; and (2) conduct a follow-up capability assessment to determine that the model's capabilities fall sufficiently far away from those Capability Thresholds, following the procedures outlined in Section 3.
paraphrase: While upgrading a model to the Required Safeguards, the policy will be updated with any additional insufficient Capability Thresholds and a follow-up capability assessment will confirm sufficient distance from those thresholds, per Section 3 procedures.

excerpt: To summarize the commitments and procedures outlined above, we may deploy or store a model if either of the following criteria are met: (1) the model's capabilities are sufficiently far away from the existing Capability Thresholds, making the current ASL-2 Standard appropriate;
paraphrase: Deployment or storage may continue if the model's capabilities are sufficiently far from existing Capability Thresholds, keeping the ASL-2 Standard appropriate.

context_stem: we may deploy or store a model if either of the following criteria are met:
excerpt: or (2) the model's capabilities have surpassed the existing Capabilities Threshold, but we have implemented the ASL-3 Required Safeguards and confirmed that the model is sufficiently far away from the next set of Capability Thresholds as to make the model ASL-3 Standard appropriate.
paraphrase: Alternatively, deployment/storage may continue if capabilities exceed the existing threshold but ASL-3 Required Safeguards are implemented and sufficient distance from the next thresholds is confirmed.

excerpt: We may also continue to train more capable models, conducting preliminary and comprehensive assessments as before.
paraphrase: More capable models may continue to be trained, with preliminary and comprehensive assessments conducted as before.

excerpt: In any scenario where we determine that a model requires ASL-3 Required Safeguards but we are unable to implement them immediately, we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place:
paraphrase: If ASL-3 Required Safeguards are needed but cannot be implemented immediately, prompt action will reduce interim risk until the safeguards are ready.

context_stem: we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place:
excerpt: Interim measures: The CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer may approve the use of interim measures that provide the same level of assurance as the relevant ASL-3 Standard but are faster or simpler to implement.
paraphrase: The CEO and RSO may approve interim measures giving equivalent assurance to the ASL-3 Standard but quicker or simpler to implement.

excerpt: In the deployment context, such measures might include blocking model responses, downgrading to a less-capable model in a particular domain, or increasing the sensitivity of automated monitoring.
paraphrase: Deployment-context interim measures might include blocking responses, downgrading models in a domain, or increasing monitoring sensitivity.

excerpt: In the security context, an example of such a measure would be storing the model weights in a single-purpose, isolated network that meets the ASL-3 Standard.
paraphrase: In the security context, an example measure is storing weights in an isolated single-purpose network meeting the ASL-3 Standard.

excerpt: In either case, the CEO and Responsible Scaling Officer will share their plan with the Board of Directors and the Long-Term Benefit Trust.
paraphrase: Either way, the CEO and RSO will share the interim measures plan with the Board and Long-Term Benefit Trust.

context_stem: we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place:
excerpt: Stronger restrictions: In the unlikely event that we cannot implement interim measures to adequately mitigate risk, we will impose stronger restrictions.
paraphrase: If interim measures cannot adequately mitigate risk, stronger restrictions will be imposed.

excerpt: In the deployment context, we will de-deploy the model and replace it with a model that falls below the Capability Threshold. Once the ASL-3 Deployment Standard can be met, the model may be re-deployed.
paraphrase: In deployment, the model will be withdrawn and replaced by one below the Capability Threshold, with re-deployment possible once the ASL-3 Deployment Standard is met.

excerpt: In the security context, we will delete model weights. Given the availability of interim deployment and security protections, however, stronger restrictions should rarely be necessary.
paraphrase: In the security context, model weights will be deleted, though stronger restrictions should rarely be needed given available interim protections.

context_stem: we will act promptly to reduce interim risk to acceptable levels until the ASL-3 Required Safeguards are in place:
excerpt: Monitoring pretraining: We will not train models with comparable or greater capabilities to the one that requires the ASL-3 Security Standard.
paraphrase: Models with comparable or greater capabilities to the one requiring the ASL-3 Security Standard will not be trained.

excerpt: This is achieved by monitoring the capabilities of the model in pretraining and comparing them against the given model.
paraphrase: This is done by monitoring pretraining model capabilities and comparing them to the reference model.

excerpt: If the pretraining model's capabilities are comparable or greater, we will pause training until we have implemented the ASL-3 Security Standard and established it is sufficient for the model.
paraphrase: If pretraining capabilities are comparable or greater, training will pause until the ASL-3 Security Standard is implemented and confirmed sufficient.

excerpt: We will set expectations with internal stakeholders about the potential for such pauses.
paraphrase: Internal stakeholders will be given expectations about the possibility of such training pauses.

excerpt: When choosing amongst options that satisfy the safety criteria, we will implement whichever interim safeguards minimize changes to customer experience.
paraphrase: Among safety-satisfying options, the interim safeguards chosen will be those minimizing customer experience changes.

excerpt: We consider implementation of the ASL-3 Security Standard alone sufficient to continue training, regardless of whether the ASL-3 Deployment Standard is satisfied.
paraphrase: Implementing the ASL-3 Security Standard alone is considered sufficient to continue training, irrespective of the Deployment Standard.

excerpt: "Comparable or greater capabilities" is operationalized as 1x or more in Effective Compute.
paraphrase: The term "comparable or greater capabilities" is defined as 1x or more Effective Compute.
